subject: Pilot Onramp: Stream + Toolcall + Structured Outputs for Vectra Health
messages:
From: Asha Reddy <asha@vectrahealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@vectrahealth.com>
Date: 2028-03-14T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot Onramp Request: Stream + Toolcall + JSON outputs

Hi Jordan / Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited. We’d like to kick off a small pilot to validate: streaming live transcriptions into our triage flow, using a toolcall to enrich with our patient metadata service, and asserting a strict JSON output shape for downstream ingestion.

Scope (first pass):
- 2-week pilot; up to 100k generated tokens/day
- Streaming responses into our endpoint (we’ll provide a test webhook)
- One toolcall: fetch patient metadata (ID -> demographics + current plan)
- Structured JSON output: fixed keys for `intent`, `entities`, `summary` (we attached a rough schema)

Can you confirm what level of support Redwood will provide for: schema validation, any runtime adapter we need for toolcalls, and an SLO for 99th-percentile token latency?

Attached: pilot-scope.xlsx (outline + sample records)

Proposed kickoff window: Tue 21 Mar or Wed 22 Mar morning PT.

Asha Reddy
Program Manager, Integrations
Vectra Health

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Asha Reddy <asha@vectrahealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-03-14T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot Onramp Request: Stream + Toolcall + JSON outputs

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear scope, this is straightforward to run as a pilot. High-level answers up front:
- Schema validation: we can run schema checks server-side and surface mismatches in the Console; we’ll also add a lightweight preflight validator you can run against samples.
- Runtime adapter: Redwood supports function/tool calling; for your patient metadata service we can onboard a simple HTTP tool integration (auth via API key or mTLS).
- Latency SLO: for pilot infra we target 99p token latency <= 220ms on our hosted cluster; we’ll validate in the first 48 hours and adjust if needed.

Proposed kickoff: Tue 2028-03-21 09:00 PT (30–45 min). Agenda: introductions, test endpoints, sample payloads & schema alignment, acceptance criteria.

Can Tom and any devs join for the test endpoint handoff? Monica, Ben — I’d like you two on the call for the runtime + infra pieces. Soojin, looping you for schema gate thoughts.

Jordan Blake
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Asha Reddy <asha@vectrahealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@vectrahealth.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-03-14T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot Onramp Request: Pilot details + sample schema

Asha — attaching a lightweight example JSON schema in the body below to align expectations. We prefer strict shape checks for the pilot to avoid downstream regressions. If you have a sample record set I can run the preflight locally and share mismatches before the call.

Example expected output (informal):
{
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["intent","entities","summary","metadata"],
  "properties": {
    "intent": {"type":"string"},
    "entities": {"type":"array","items":{"type":"object"}},
    "summary": {"type":"string"},
    "metadata": {"type":"object","properties":{"patient_id":{"type":"string"},"source":{"type":"string"}}}
  }
}

On the streaming/toolcall mapping: we’ll maintain a consistent request envelope from your webhook to our runtime; when a toolcall is invoked we return a short JSON payload (max 2KB) which the model can reference. We recommend returning normalized keys (e.g., patient_id, plan_type) to keep the structured output deterministic.

I’ll bring an example adapter (simple node express snippet) to the call.

Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Asha Reddy <asha@vectrahealth.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@vectrahealth.com>
Date: 2028-03-14T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot Onramp Request: infra, SLOs and acceptance criteria

Quick infra notes from my side:
- For the pilot we’ll provision a single dedicated pool (shared pilot nodes) with autoscale capped to ensure predictable latency.
- Network: we can use TLS + API key; if you require mTLS we’ll coordinate keys ahead of time.
- Monitoring: please expect token-level latency metrics surfaced in the Console and a short-term Dashboard I’ll share.

Suggested acceptance criteria (sample):
1) Successful end-to-end flows for 100 messages, with schema validation >= 95%
2) 99p token latency <= 220ms over 24h test window
3) Toolcall success rate >= 99% (retries handled by Redwood runtime)

Attaching pilot-checklist.pdf (checkpoints + owner map). Jordan — I added a quick ops play for rollback and for pinning to a fallback model if needed.

Ben Carter
Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@vectrahealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Asha Reddy <asha@vectrahealth.com>
Date: 2028-03-14T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot Onramp Request: confirmed kickoff + SOW

Jordan / team — thanks, that all looks good. Tue 21 Mar 09:00 PT works for us. Devs from our side: me and Priya Rao (CC’d on the calendar invite).

We’ll sign the small SOW and return via DocuSign today — attaching SOW-Vectra-2028.pdf for reference. Please send the DocuSign link and the meeting invite when ready.
